notes:
Summary: small DTC apparel + gifts shop. Primarily product pages + email chat widget. Wants hosted API to avoid infra ops.

Key needs / constraints:
- Primary: product Q&A on PDPs (single-turn Q&A + short chat), reduce support tickets
- Secondary: catalog enrichment (auto-tags, variant mapping) to improve search relevance
- Traffic pattern: low steady traffic but sharp bursts during promos and weekend drops — worried about per-token cost spikes
- Latency target: <200ms median for Q&A on product pages; acceptable up to 400ms for background enrichment jobs
- Cost sensitivity: very price-conscious; prefers predictable per-month spend or low initial commit; will likely stay on pay-as-you-go and upgrade if ROI clear
- Model preference: open to small/quantized variants for cost (gpt-small-like / 7B-ish), want a fallback to higher-quality model for ambiguous queries
- Routing/fallback: wants simple rule — use small model for known SKUs, fallback to higher-cost model for unknown queries or when confidence low
- Security/compliance: public cloud OK; wants audit logs and short retention (30–90 days). No heavy regulated-data flows. KMS for API keys desirable but not blocking

Quotes from Ana (founder): "We need something we can plug in this week that doesn't blow our margins. If it reduces even 10 support tickets a week it's worth it."

POC plan proposed:
- Week 0: give 7-day sandbox + sample ingest script (already sent)
- Week 1: index core catalog (500–1,200 SKUs), demo Q&A on PDP, measure median latency and token usage
- Week 2: validate fallback behavior and run 3 simulated promo bursts (load test) to check throttling and cost delta
- Acceptance: 2-week trial showing support ticket reduction on small A/B (chat widget vs control)

Open questions / AE notes:
- Need to provide clear small-model latency & cost benchmarks (pick 2-3 model variants) — ask infra team for quick perf table
- Provide example batching and caching guidance for bursty widget traffic (prefix caching helps for common product queries)
- Confirm whether auto-scaling burst protection via Dedicated bursting is available for SMB — likely not; highlight rate-limits + client-side retry/backoff
